Maintain consistent derivative orientation and training/validation splits.

content.family: Reverse-mode differentiation through a finite gradient-descent trajectory

limitations.statement: The output differentiates a finite GD trajectory for the supplied batch; it need not equal the exact bilevel hypergradient or the full-task sum for a strict subset B.
Neither Algorithm 1 nor the recorded global-minimizer consistency Theorem supplies an outer-optimization iteration bound or unrestricted Oracle Complexity bound.

variants.cost: Execution ledger from the displayed loops, not a source Oracle Complexity theorem: per episode, T training-gradient evaluations; validation partial gradients in w and lambda at one endpoint, possibly jointly evaluated; T mixed-derivative row products and T Hessian row products; vector updates and batch summation also require computation. Stored-trajectory execution retains needed w_t^j states plus current adjoint and p^j. Derivative-product access avoids full Hessian storage. Sequential episode processing permits workspace reuse. Recomputing discarded states adds forward-gradient work and must be charged. No unit-cost equivalence between gradients, derivative products, data passes, arithmetic or memory is assumed.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Main PDF p.3 Eqs.(5),(6); p.5 Algorithm 1 and Eqs.(9),(10).
variants.name: Algorithm 1: Reverse-HG for Hyper-representation
variants.output: Return sum_{j in B} p^j, the lambda derivative of sum_{j in B} L^j(w_T^j(lambda),lambda,D_val^j) for fixed B, eta, T and data. This is a sum, not a mean. Taking B to contain every task gives the Eq.(9) finite-task objective gradient.
public_inputs: Shared lambda in R^m; positive integer T; fixed ground learning rate eta; supplied finite episode batch B, each episode having fixed training and validation splits.
Task losses L^j(w,lambda,S). This variant does not differentiate dependence of eta, T or batch selection on lambda.
variants.query_and_update: For j in B and t=1,...,T, query g_t^j=partial_w L^j(w_{t-1}^j,lambda,D_tr^j), then set w_t^j=w_{t-1}^j-eta*g_t^j. Reverse for t=T-1,...,0: p^j <- p^j-eta*alpha_{t+1}^j*B_t^j; alpha_t^j <- alpha_{t+1}^j*(I-eta*H_t^j). Both operations use the old alpha_{t+1}^j. Here H_t^j=D_w(partial_w L^j)(w_t^j,lambda,D_tr^j) has shape d_j×d_j and B_t^j=D_lambda(partial_w L^j)(w_t^j,lambda,D_tr^j) has shape d_j×m. Derivative products can be evaluated without materializing the full matrices.
variants.requirements: Section 2.3 uses smooth dynamics. The displayed GD rule requires the training w Hessian and w/lambda mixed derivative and validation w and lambda partial gradients along the trajectory; C² training and C¹ validation losses suffice. Exact derivative products are required for exact finite-trajectory differentiation. Strong convexity and convergence of inner GD are not needed merely to execute the rule.
variants.state_and_initialization: For every j in B, initialize w_0^j=0 in R^{d_j}; hold lambda, eta and episode data fixed. Retain or faithfully recompute the trajectory for the reverse pass. At the endpoint initialize row alpha_T^j=partial_w L^j(w_T^j,lambda,D_val^j) and row p^j=partial_lambda L^j(w_T^j,lambda,D_val^j), taking these partial derivatives at fixed w_T^j.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: T and eta are supplied inputs. Execute exactly T forward and T reverse iterations per episode. Algorithm 1 specifies no accuracy-based choice of T, outer step size, outer stopping criterion or batch-size guarantee. Inner convergence conditions are separate obligations when applying a consistency Theorem.
